top.title: Cheap decision models start replacing frontier LLMs for classification and rubric scoring
top.summary: Google launched the Gemini Decisions API, which answers up to 1,000 yes/no, multiple-choice or rubric questions about text, images, audio, video or PDFs in one pass for $0.10 per 2M input tokens, with free output. Separately, Amazon swapped Claude Sonnet for its own Strands Decider model on internal ticket labeling, matching accuracy at about 98% lower cost while running both side by side so it could roll back in 45 seconds.
top.why: Many PMM workflow steps are really classification or rubric checks (tagging CI signals, scoring drafts against a messaging checklist), so routing those to a decision model could cut cost and add a consistent, auditable QA gate.

top.title: Managing coding agents looks a lot like managing a team, and the playbook transfers
top.summary: An essay by Anthropic's Addy Osmani lays out how to work with agents: give each one a way to check its own work, state the goal and definition of done, write any correction you make twice into CLAUDE.md or a shared skill, and track quality and rework instead of the share of AI-written output.
top.why: This is a ready-made operating standard for the PMM skills library: a definition of done per workflow, a rule for when a fix becomes a skill update, and rework rate as the quality metric.

top.title: Claude Projects can now write their own knowledge files
top.summary: Claude Projects on the web can now save research and summaries as new knowledge files, so a scheduled task can gather information and add it to a shared Project over time instead of needing a local setup.
top.why: A scheduled competitor-watch task that saves weekly findings into a shared Project gives the CI program a running, team-visible record that later prompts and battlecard updates can draw on.

try_this.title: Assumption audit for AI-generated analysis
try_this.how: After Claude produces an analysis (win-rate summary, adoption numbers, competitor comparison), ask it to list every definition and assumption it used, then paste only your original request and that list into a fresh chat and ask where each term is narrower, broader or different from what you asked. Try it on one recurring report this week and see if it catches a quiet scope change.

workflows.title: incident.io replaced its ads agency with an AI skill for ABM launches
workflows.summary: A roundup of working GTM plays says incident.io cut ABM campaign launches from 2-3 days to about 3 minutes with an AI skill, and Vercel doubled its field event cadence with an internal app that automates invites, seating and follow-up.
workflows.why: These are concrete, named examples of marketing teams automating the manual work around channels that already convert, useful as benchmarks when scoping the next PMM workflow.

workflows.title: Grok Bot 1.0 puts shared agent teammates in Slack, Teams and meetings
workflows.summary: xAI moved Grok Bot out of beta: teams can share bots that join video calls, Slack and Microsoft Teams, learn how the team works, and flag unfinished work on their own.
workflows.why: Team-shared agents that live in chat and meetings are becoming standard across vendors, which shapes how a PMM 'AI concierge' should be delivered.

workflows.title: Claude Fable 5.2 now available in Microsoft Copilot Cowork and Copilot Studio
workflows.summary: Microsoft added Anthropic's newest model to Copilot Cowork and Copilot Studio, so Copilot users can now pick among models from three rival labs.
workflows.why: If parts of the org are on Microsoft 365, Claude-based workflows may be portable into Copilot Studio without a separate Claude seat.

governance.title: Fireworks AI breach exposed Notion AI chats despite zero-data-retention claims
governance.summary: Attackers who reached Fireworks AI's stored batch inference data exposed Notion AI chat transcripts for under 1% of workspaces, even though the data was covered by 'zero data retention' terms.
governance.why: A useful case for Legal and Security reviews: ask vendors where batch and async jobs are stored, not only whether real-time prompts are retained.

governance.title: United Airlines blocks unauthorized AI agents from booking
governance.summary: United restricted third-party AI agents from its site, app and outside booking channels, citing exposed logins, accidental purchases and rules that require a human sign-off; Walmart is taking the opposite path with permissioned agent profiles and spending limits.
governance.why: Companies are now choosing between blocking agents and granting them scoped permissions with human approval, a live example of the human-in-the-loop control story Camunda tells.

competitive.title: n8n previews Nod, a self-hosted personal agent
competitive.summary: n8n released Nod as a free, open-source research preview: a personal agent that runs on your own machine or server and handles tasks like chasing invoices, canceling trials and writing pre-call briefs.
competitive.why: CI signal: a workflow automation neighbor is moving from builder tooling into packaged personal agents, worth tracking for battlecards.

competitive.title: Rivian used agents on Bedrock to clear manual ERP accrual work
competitive.summary: AWS describes how Rivian's finance team replaced 15+ days per cycle of manual purchase-order accrual work with agents that read plain-language SOPs and route decisions by dollar threshold.
competitive.why: A reference story for agentic process automation in finance, the kind of SOP-driven, threshold-routed process Camunda positions orchestration for.

measurement.title: Le Monde: ChatGPT referrals convert to paid at 260x the rate of Google Discover
measurement.summary: Le Monde's CEO says readers who arrive via ChatGPT citations become paying subscribers at about 260 times the rate of Google Discover traffic, so the publisher treats AI citations as a distribution channel.
measurement.why: Supports tracking AI-assistant referrals as their own channel with conversion quality, not just volume, in marketing dashboards.

landscape.title: Nvidia board weighs replacing CEO Jensen Huang
landscape.summary: Nvidia's board is reportedly preparing to remove Huang and has hired an outside firm to find candidates after reports of two affairs; the stock fell about 8% after hours.

landscape.title: OpenAI posts its first $10B quarter
landscape.summary: OpenAI's Q3 revenue reportedly topped $10B, up about 50% from Q2, driven by enterprise adoption of its models and agent tools.
